recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed for FHIR-25556 unless Patient Care later decides that the example value set should use a different SNOMED expression or include the 405533003 grouping concept itself.
issue_request: FHIR-25556 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking that AdverseEvent.outcome stop using the overly strict preferred binding to the NCI UMLS value set and instead use an example binding to SNOMED CT adverse incident outcome categories under SCTID 405533003.
initial_application: Commit c31023666df8a405c7dd87ba90542d2eb32b7154 applied J#25556 by changing the then-authoritative AdverseEvent spreadsheet outcome binding from preferred to example and replacing the NCI value set compose with a SNOMED CT hierarchy filter rooted at 405533003. This followed FHIR-23022, which had introduced the preferred NCI binding that FHIR-25556 later relaxed.
additional_context: AdverseEvent remains in current build scope through source/fhir.ini, with Patient Care ownership. Later source refactoring moved the resource definition into source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml while preserving the example binding and SNOMED CT adverse-event-outcome value set. Patient Care minutes from 2020-01-02 record the same action item to change outcome to an example SNOMED binding for international implementers; searched Zulip evidence did not reveal a conflicting binding decision.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml binds AdverseEvent.outcome with strength example to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/adverse-event-outcome, and source/adverseevent/valueset-adverse-event-outcome.xml composes SNOMED CT descendants of 405533003.
